stem: Deepak starts from point A. He walks 10 km East, then 6 km North, then 10 km West, then 8 km South. How far and in which direction is he now from point A?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 2 km North uses the correct magnitude but the wrong direction; the southward distance (8) exceeds northward (6), so net is South not North.
4 km South comes from subtracting 6-8 but taking the result from the wrong starting point, or using 10-6 as the south displacement.
8 km South ignores the 6 km North leg; only the southward leg was used without subtracting the northward offset.

explanation: Resolve displacements along each axis. East-West: 10 km East minus 10 km West = 0 net. North-South: 6 km North minus 8 km South = 2 km net South. So Deepak is 2 km due South of A.

explanation_sections.punchline: East cancels West; 8 South minus 6 North leaves 2 km net South.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: split into two independent axes. EW axis: +10-10=0. NS axis: +6-8=-2 (i.e., 2 South). Final displacement = 2 km South. No Pythagoras needed since EW net is zero.
explanation_sections.lesson: Resolve multi-leg routes axis by axis. Opposite-direction legs on the same axis cancel. Only if both net components are non-zero is Pythagoras required.
explanation_sections.timing: 45-55 seconds. The main traps are forgetting the opposite-axis cancellation (gives 8 km South, option 4) and reversing the North/South result (gives 2 km North, option 2).
